candidates.original_title: Kinase-dead BRAF and oncogenic RAS cooperate to drive tumor progression through CRAF
candidates.description: Paradoxical activation of MEK/ERK signaling by BRAF inhibitors (PLX4720, 885-A) in BRAF[WT]/NRAS[Q61L] D04 cells, and lack of activation by sorafenib
candidates.citation_sentence: In their 2010 paper, Heidorn and colleagues examined the mechanism of action behind this paradoxical activation of MEK/ERK signaling.
candidates.notes: Registered report protocol paper; replication results reported in a separate paper; Protocol 1 replicates Figure 1A of Heidorn et al.

candidates.original_title: Kinase-dead BRAF and oncogenic RAS cooperate to drive tumor progression through CRAF
candidates.description: Knockdown of NRAS or CRAF abrogates paradoxical MEK/ERK activation by 885-A in D04 cells
candidates.citation_sentence: In their 2010 paper, Heidorn and colleagues examined the mechanism of action behind this paradoxical activation of MEK/ERK signaling.
candidates.notes: Registered report protocol paper; replication results reported in a separate paper; Protocol 2 replicates Figure 1B of Heidorn et al.

candidates.notes: Registered report protocol paper; replication results reported in a separate paper; Protocol 3 replicates Figure 3A of Heidorn et al.

candidates.description: BRAF[R188L] mutant does not bind to CRAF even in the presence of drug-induced RAS activity

candidates.notes: Registered report protocol paper; replication results reported in a separate paper; Protocol 4 replicates Figure 3B of Heidorn et al.

candidates.original_title: Kinase-dead BRAF and oncogenic RAS cooperate to drive tumor progression through CRAF
candidates.description: Kinase-dead BRAF[D594A] still binds to CRAF, indicating that inhibition of BRAF activity drives BRAF binding to CRAF and paradoxical activation
candidates.citation_sentence: In their 2010 paper, Heidorn and colleagues examined the mechanism of action behind this paradoxical activation of MEK/ERK signaling.
candidates.notes: Registered report protocol paper; replication results reported in a separate paper; Protocol 5 replicates Figure 4D of Heidorn et al.

candidates.original_title: Kinase-dead BRAF and oncogenic RAS cooperate to drive tumor progression through CRAF
candidates.description: Heidorn et al.'s Figure 1A claimed that RAF inhibitors block MEK/ERK activation in BRAF[V600E] cells but fail to repress and can paradoxically activate MEK/ERK signaling in BRAF[WT] cells with activated NRAS, as tested in Protocol 1.
candidates.citation_sentence: In their 2010 paper, Heidorn and colleagues examined the mechanism of action behind this paradoxical activation of MEK/ERK signaling. In Figure 1A, Heidorn and colleagues examined pathway activation in response to a range of drugs.
candidates.notes: Registered-report protocol; replication outcomes are not reported, so the result is inconclusive. Protocol 1 uses D04 and A375 cells, replaces 885-A with SB590885, and excludes some original cell lines and drugs. [luna56: extra entry, not in the external record]

candidates.original_title: Kinase-dead BRAF and oncogenic RAS cooperate to drive tumor progression through CRAF
candidates.description: Heidorn et al.'s Figure 1B claimed that NRAS or CRAF knockdown abrogates 885-A-induced MEK/ERK activation in D04 cells, as tested in Protocol 2.
candidates.citation_sentence: In their 2010 paper, Heidorn and colleagues examined the mechanism of action behind this paradoxical activation of MEK/ERK signaling. To determine if CRAF was required for paradoxical pathway activation, Heidorn and colleagues treated D04 cells with siRNAs targeting NRAS and CRAF.
candidates.notes: Registered-report protocol; replication outcomes are not reported, so the result is inconclusive. Protocol 2 replaces 885-A with SB590885. [luna56: extra entry, not in the external record]

candidates.original_title: Kinase-dead BRAF and oncogenic RAS cooperate to drive tumor progression through CRAF
candidates.description: Heidorn et al.'s Figure 3A claimed that drug-induced BRAF/CRAF heterodimerization requires active RAS signaling, such that the RAS-binding-deficient CRAF[R89L] mutant cannot bind BRAF, as tested in Protocol 3.
candidates.citation_sentence: In their 2010 paper, Heidorn and colleagues examined the mechanism of action behind this paradoxical activation of MEK/ERK signaling. Since activated RAS is known to drive heterodimerization of BRAF and CRAF (Weber et al., 2001), Heidorn and colleagues also tested if drug binding drove heterodimerization of BRAF and CRAF, and if this heterodimerization was dependent on active RAS signaling.
candidates.notes: Registered-report protocol; replication outcomes are not reported, so the result is inconclusive. Protocol 3 changes the transfection method and replaces 885-A with SB590885. [luna56: extra entry, not in the external record]

candidates.original_title: Kinase-dead BRAF and oncogenic RAS cooperate to drive tumor progression through CRAF
candidates.description: Heidorn et al.'s Figure 3B claimed that inhibitor treatment promotes binding of wild-type BRAF to CRAF, whereas the RAS-binding-deficient BRAF[R188L] mutant does not bind CRAF even after inhibitor treatment, as tested in Protocol 4.
candidates.citation_sentence: In their 2010 paper, Heidorn and colleagues examined the mechanism of action behind this paradoxical activation of MEK/ERK signaling. The authors showed that BRAF binds to CRAF but only in the presence of WT RAS, not oncogenic RAS.
candidates.notes: Registered-report protocol; replication outcomes are not reported, so the result is inconclusive. Protocol 4 changes the transfection method and replaces 885-A with SB590885. [luna56: extra entry, not in the external record]

candidates.original_title: Kinase-dead BRAF and oncogenic RAS cooperate to drive tumor progression through CRAF
candidates.description: Heidorn et al.'s Figure 4D claimed that kinase-dead BRAF[D594A] binds CRAF, showing that inhibition of BRAF activity rather than drug binding itself drives BRAF/CRAF association, as tested in Protocol 5.
candidates.citation_sentence: In their 2010 paper, Heidorn and colleagues examined the mechanism of action behind this paradoxical activation of MEK/ERK signaling. After confirming that drug binding to BRAF drove BRAF binding to CRAF, Heidorn and colleagues tested a kinase dead version of BRAF (BRAF[D594A]) (Figure 4D).
candidates.notes: Registered-report protocol; replication outcomes are not reported, so the result is inconclusive. [luna56: extra entry, not in the external record]
